Studies may omit tests for reasons associated with their accuracy.
NMADTA provides missing-not-at-random (MNAR) functions to examine how results
change under alternative missingness assumptions.

## Available functions

- [`nmadt.hierarchical.MNAR()`](../reference/nmadt.hierarchical.MNAR.html)
  extends the hierarchical formulation.
- [`nmadt.hsroc.MNAR()`](../reference/nmadt.hsroc.MNAR.html)
  extends the HSROC formulation.

The input uses the [same column structure](data-format.html) as the
regular fitting functions.

## Sensitivity parameters

`gamma1` and `gamma0` are numeric vectors of length `K`. They describe the
dependence of missingness on test sensitivity and specificity, respectively,
on the model's logit scale.

The reference recommends treating them as sensitivity-analysis parameters.
Zero represents no dependence on the corresponding accuracy parameter;
negative values can represent poorer-performing tests being more likely
to be missing under this selection model.

~~~r
library(NMADTA)
data(dat.kang)

fit_mnar <- nmadt.hierarchical.MNAR(
  nstu = 12, K = 2, data = dat.kang,
  testname = c("D-dimer", "Ultrasonography"),
  gamma1 = c(-0.5, -0.5),
  gamma0 = c(-0.5, -0.5),
  directory = tempdir(),
  n.adapt = 5000, n.iter = 50000, n.chains = 3,
  conv.diag = TRUE
)
summary(fit_mnar)
~~~

## Compare several assumptions

Repeat the fit over a prespecified grid. Here each grid value is applied
to both tests and to both accuracy coefficients:

~~~r
gamma_grid <- c(0, -0.5, -1, -2)
fits <- lapply(gamma_grid, function(g) {
  nmadt.hierarchical.MNAR(
    nstu = 12, K = 2, data = dat.kang,
    testname = c("D-dimer", "Ultrasonography"),
    gamma1 = rep(g, 2), gamma0 = rep(g, 2),
    directory = tempdir(),
    n.adapt = 5000, n.iter = 50000, n.chains = 3,
    conv.diag = TRUE
  )
})
names(fits) <- paste0("gamma_", gamma_grid)
lapply(fits, summary)
~~~

These values illustrate the workflow. Choose plausible assumptions for
your review, document them, and check convergence for each fit.
The observed data alone do not identify the missingness mechanism.

See the [reference](../reference/nmadt.hierarchical.MNAR.html) for the complete
arguments and the [article](https://doi.org/10.1017/rsm.2026.10097) for examples.
